Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.

Coverage and verification procedure:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, their approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps,
and uncertain or occluded regions. These are estimates from this input, not calibration.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. A valid
hierarchy verifies only the parts you emitted; it does not establish image completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible parts because they are small.
For composite objects, match the overall silhouette and the distribution of occupied space
and gaps before adding fine repeated details. Estimate component sizes relative to their
parent and nearby objects from the reference. A correct outer bounding box alone does not
ensure the correct internal density, component proportions or visible coverage. Keep these
parameters explicit so that a later revision can change them without rebuilding the design.

Use the first execution for a complete scene, leaving the second available for correction.
After a successful render, compare the reference inventory against the full rendered view:
missing or extra visible parts, silhouette, internal gaps, relative sizes, overlaps and image
bounds. Identify the largest supported discrepancies before revising. If many objects share
a displacement or scale error, consider camera/framing; if a discrepancy is local, consider
that object's parameters. Neither pattern proves a unique cause. Preserve matching objects
and their editable hierarchy while correcting the supported discrepancies. Do not impose
one fixed density, camera, object count or parameter adjustment across different inputs.
An isolated-object view, if supplied, can clarify membership and silhouette, but its full-image
score is not evidence that removing the rest of the scene improves the reconstruction.
Keep unresolved mappings and occluded geometry explicitly uncertain.

The entire solve has three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds. A short
Python loop can generate thousands of Blender objects before any image exists. Plan a
compact complete first build so that realization and the runner's render can finish with
time for review. Do not change the runner's resource policy or rendering settings to evade
this budget. Use geometry complexity as the controllable cost.

mesh and marker; a fillet_box can expand to 26 primitives; sweep_tube with n points emits

heuristic rather than a measured runtime guarantee or fixed object count. Allocate detail

and its meaningful editable parts. Represent unresolved surface detail with shared materials
and restrained procedural shading; retain geometric detail that changes visible contours,

Use short, adaptively spaced tube paths for visible curves, concentrating points at bends.
Avoid many nearly identical Boolean slices to approximate one hollow shape; use a small

coverage or appearance defects from a timeout. A reduced-cost build still needs execution
and rendered-image verification; simplification alone is not evidence of success.

feedback: do not treat it as evidence for unrelated camera or geometry changes. Preserve

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

```python
# Reference inventory and visual anchors, estimated from the supplied composite:
# - The control-room photograph occupies the lower portion of the reference.
#   Its back wall has pale rectangular cabinets and a regular grid of square
#   instruments; a dark horizontal ventilation grille is near its center.
# - A long foreground console runs diagonally across the photograph, from the
#   cropped lower-left toward the back-right. Its light sloping control panels
#   contain many dark switches and meters; a dark base supports them.
# - A smaller pale console stands against the right wall, with a dark base.
# - The yellow GRID board shown above the room photograph is a separate reference
#   to be incorporated into the room; its exact original room position is unknown.
# - The room photograph's important relative anchors, normalized to that photograph:
#   back-wall upper-left (0.00, 0.00), grille center (0.35, 0.36),
#   console near-left contour (0.03, 0.89), console far-right end (0.70, 0.40),
#   small console top (0.90, 0.43). These are approximate visual correspondences.
# - Dominant edges: back wall is nearly horizontal; the console long edges rise
#   strongly toward the right; cabinet verticals are nearly vertical.
# - The console overlaps the lower wall instruments. Rear corners and ceiling are
#   partially cropped, so the unobserved extent of the room is uncertain.
#
# Expanded geometry estimate: architecture ~8 boxes; wall cabinets and instruments
# ~125 boxes; main console body and controls ~150 boxes/rods; right console ~35;
# GRID board and diagram ~55; lights ~5. Total approximately 380 primitives.
# Tiny labels and repeated markings are intentionally simplified.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math
from mathutils import Vector

scene = Scene("1970s_Grid_Control_Room")

# Major room and console parameters, independently editable.
ROOM_W = 9.2
ROOM_D = 6.7
ROOM_H = 3.35
CONSOLE_X0, CONSOLE_X1 = -4.25, 2.20
CONSOLE_Y = -0.65
CONSOLE_Z = 0.90
CAMERA_POSITION = (-7.5, -10.5, 5.1)
CAMERA_TARGET = (-0.15, 1.0, 1.38)
CAMERA_LENS = 35

wall = (0.73, 0.71, 0.66)
wall_light = (0.82, 0.80, 0.75)
cabinet = (0.73, 0.72, 0.68)
panel = (0.79, 0.78, 0.72)
paper = (0.87, 0.85, 0.78)
dark = (0.12, 0.12, 0.11)
base = (0.22, 0.21, 0.19)
yellow = (0.95, 0.70, 0.13)
red = (0.75, 0.035, 0.025)
amber = (0.95, 0.48, 0.035)
black = (0.045, 0.045, 0.04)

architecture = Asset("Architecture")
architecture.include("Floor", box((ROOM_W, ROOM_D, 0.12), (0, 0, -0.06), (0.38, 0.36, 0.32)))
architecture.include("Back_wall", box((ROOM_W, 0.12, ROOM_H), (0, 3.3, ROOM_H/2), wall_light))
architecture.include("Right_wall", box((0.12, ROOM_D, ROOM_H), (4.6, 0, ROOM_H/2), wall))
architecture.include("Ceiling", box((ROOM_W, ROOM_D, 0.10), (0, 0, ROOM_H), wall_light))
architecture.include("Back_baseboard", box((ROOM_W, 0.05, 0.16), (0, 3.20, 0.08), base))
scene.include("Architecture", architecture)

# Back wall instrument bank: regular cabinet bays and visible square instruments.
bank = Asset("Main_wall_instrument_bank")
bank.include("Cabinet_backing", box((6.5, 0.16, 2.45), (-1.15, 3.18, 1.48), cabinet))
for i in range(9):
    x = -4.15 + i * 0.76
    bank.include("Cabinet_seam_%02d" % i,
                 box((0.015, 0.018, 2.35), (x, 3.085, 1.50), (0.41, 0.40, 0.37)))
# Left and right clusters; center is occupied by the ventilation grille.
for col in list(range(5)) + list(range(8, 11)):
    x = -3.92 + col * 0.49
    for row in range(4):
        z = 1.12 + row * 0.40
        bank.include("Meter_frame_%02d_%02d" % (col, row),
                     box((0.31, 0.035, 0.29), (x, 3.065, z), dark))
        bank.include("Meter_face_%02d_%02d" % (col, row),
                     box((0.245, 0.012, 0.225), (x, 3.040, z), paper))
        bank.include("Meter_needle_%02d_%02d" % (col, row),
                     box((0.012, 0.008, 0.095), (x + 0.01, 3.030, z), dark))
bank.include("Grille_surround", box((1.30, 0.045, 0.74), (-1.12, 3.05, 1.72), panel))
for j in range(8):
    bank.include("Grille_slit_%02d" % j,
                 box((1.13, 0.02, 0.035), (-1.12, 3.018, 1.46 + j*0.073), dark))
scene.include("Main_wall_instrument_bank", bank)

# Main console: a horizontal writing shelf in front of an inclined control face.
console = Asset("Main_sloped_control_console")
length = CONSOLE_X1 - CONSOLE_X0
cx = (CONSOLE_X0 + CONSOLE_X1) / 2
console.include("Dark_plinth", box((length, 1.25, 0.72), (cx, CONSOLE_Y, 0.36), base))
console.include("Front_fascia", box((length, 0.10, 0.46), (cx, CONSOLE_Y-0.64, 0.58), (0.32, 0.30, 0.27)))
console.include("Writing_shelf", box((length, 0.47, 0.07),
                                      (cx, CONSOLE_Y-0.49, 0.87), paper))
# Sloped face rises toward the back wall.
slope_angle = 23
face = box((length, 1.02, 0.085), (cx, CONSOLE_Y+0.22, 1.09), panel)
face.turn(axis="x", degrees=slope_angle)
console.include("Inclined_control_face", face)

# Surface coordinate mapping on the sloping face, including its normal offset.
a = math.radians(slope_angle)
def surface_point(x, v, lift=0.055):
    return (x, CONSOLE_Y + 0.22 + v*math.cos(a) - lift*math.sin(a),
            1.09 + v*math.sin(a) + lift*math.cos(a))

for bay in range(8):
    x = CONSOLE_X0 + 0.40 + bay*0.78
    # Narrow transverse panel seams.
    seam = box((0.014, 0.92, 0.008), surface_point(x-0.34, 0), dark)
    seam.turn(axis="x", degrees=slope_angle)
    console.include("Face_seam_%02d" % bay, seam)
    for row in range(3):
        for col in range(3):
            px = x - 0.22 + col*0.19
            v = -0.30 + row*0.28
            # A dark switch with pale mounting plate, tilted with the face.
            mounting = box((0.105, 0.085, 0.012), surface_point(px, v, 0.052), paper)
            mounting.turn(axis="x", degrees=slope_angle)
            console.include("Switch_plate_%02d_%02d_%02d" % (bay,row,col), mounting)
            p = surface_point(px, v, 0.068)
            console.include("Switch_%02d_%02d_%02d" % (bay,row,col),
                            rod(0.026, start=p,
                                end=(p[0], p[1]-0.025, p[2]+0.055), color=dark))
scene.include("Main_sloped_control_console", console)

# Small independent desk in the right rear corner.
small = Asset("Right_independent_console")
small.include("Pedestal", box((1.45, 0.78, 0.72), (3.38, 2.05, 0.36), base))
small.include("Writing_ledge", box((1.55, 0.45, 0.07), (3.38, 1.72, 0.82), paper))
small_face = box((1.55, 0.64, 0.08), (3.38, 2.11, 0.98), panel)
small_face.turn(axis="x", degrees=22)
small.include("Sloped_face", small_face)
for i in range(7):
    for j in range(2):
        x = 2.79 + i*0.19
        y = 1.99 + j*0.24
        z = 0.98 + (y-2.11)*math.tan(math.radians(22)) + 0.07
        small.include("Control_%02d_%02d" % (i,j),
                      rod(0.027, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y-0.015,z+0.05), color=dark))
scene.include("Right_independent_console", small)

# Yellow grid mimic board: graphic arrangement follows the separately pictured
# board. Its location on the right wall is an uncertain reconstruction choice.
grid = Asset("GRID_single_line_mimic_board")
grid_x, grid_y, grid_z = 2.55, 3.03, 2.15
grid.include("Yellow_panel", box((1.25, 0.075, 1.60), (grid_x, grid_y, grid_z), yellow))
front_y = grid_y - 0.046
# Main black bus and branch lines.
grid.include("Vertical_bus", box((0.035, 0.015, 1.34), (grid_x+0.10, front_y, grid_z), black))
for k, zz in enumerate((1.68, 2.12, 2.56)):
    grid.include("Cross_bus_%d" % k, box((0.60, 0.016, 0.035),
                                          (grid_x+0.10, front_y, zz), black))
for side in (-1, 1):
    for k, zz in enumerate((1.68, 2.12, 2.56)):
        xx = grid_x + 0.10 + side*0.27
        grid.include("Branch_%d_%d" % (side,k),
                     box((0.035, 0.016, 0.22), (xx, front_y, zz+0.09), black))
        grid.include("Amber_indicator_%d_%d" % (side,k),
                     box((0.09, 0.025, 0.09), (xx, front_y-0.016, zz+0.08), amber))
for i in range(4):
    z = 1.66 + i*0.35
    grid.include("Round_red_lamp_%d" % i,
                 rod(0.065, start=(grid_x-0.40, front_y-0.03, z),
                     end=(grid_x-0.40, front_y-0.07, z), color=red))
    grid.include("Selector_%d" % i,
                 rod(0.042, start=(grid_x-0.22, front_y-0.03, z),
                     end=(grid_x-0.22, front_y-0.07, z), color=black))
for i, z in enumerate((1.57, 2.73)):
    grid.include("German_label_plate_%d" % i,
                 box((0.36, 0.02, 0.10), (grid_x+0.35, front_y-0.025, z), paper))
scene.include("GRID_single_line_mimic_board", grid)

lighting = Asset("Ceiling_fluorescent_fixtures")
for i, x in enumerate((-2.5, 0.2, 2.7)):
    lighting.include("Troffer_%d" % i,
                     box((1.75, 0.46, 0.035), (x, 0.3, ROOM_H-0.07), (0.94,0.93,0.86)))
scene.include("Ceiling_fluorescent_fixtures", lighting)

realize(scene)

# Configure a neutral, softly lit 1970s room.
sc = bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("SceneWorld")
sc.world.use_nodes = True
background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get("Background")
if background is None:
    background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBackground")
output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get("World Output")
if output is None:
    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputWorld")
sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs["Background"], output.inputs["Surface"])
background.inputs["Color"].default_value = (0.72, 0.70, 0.66, 1)
background.inputs["Strength"].default_value = 0.55

set_view(CAMERA_POSITION, CAMERA_TARGET, lens=CAMERA_LENS)
area_emitter((-2.5, -1.0, 3.1), power=500, size=3.5, target=(-1, 1, 0.7))
area_emitter((2.0, 1.0, 3.1), power=450, size=3.0, target=(1, 1, 0.7))

# Preserve the reference image aspect for the projection check and the active view.
sc.render.resolution_x = 374
sc.render.resolution_y = 512
sc.render.resolution_percentage = 100
sc.render.pixel_aspect_x = 1
sc.render.pixel_aspect_y = 1

# The photograph is a wide inset of a portrait collage. Its landscape composition
# must therefore be adapted to the portrait output; the estimates below are rough
# portrait-frame targets, not calibration.
landmarks = [
    ("wall grille center", (-1.12, 3.00, 1.72), (0.37, 0.39)),
    ("console near left corner", (CONSOLE_X0, CONSOLE_Y-0.72, 0.87), (0.12, 0.73)),
    ("console far right corner", (CONSOLE_X1, CONSOLE_Y+0.68, 1.30), (0.67, 0.52)),
    ("small console top", (3.38, 2.30, 1.13), (0.82, 0.52)),
    ("yellow panel top", (grid_x, grid_y, grid_z+0.80), (0.73, 0.24)),
]
def report_landmarks():
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
    cam = sc.camera
    dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
    matrix = cam.calc_matrix_camera(
        dg, x=sc.render.resolution_x, y=sc.render.resolution_y,
        scale_x=sc.render.pixel_aspect_x, scale_y=sc.render.pixel_aspect_y)
    print("Landmark                       reference       projected")
    result = []
    for name, p, ref in landmarks:
        clip = matrix @ cam.matrix_world.inverted() @ Vector((*p, 1.0))
        uv = None if clip.w <= 1e-8 else (
            .5*(clip.x/clip.w+1), .5*(1-clip.y/clip.w))
        result.append(uv)
        print("%-30s %s %s" % (name, ref, None if uv is None else
                                (round(uv[0],3), round(uv[1],3))))
    return result

uvs = report_landmarks()
# If a confidently visible landmark is outside the frame, widen the view once.
```

```python
# Reference and feedback comparison (normalized image coordinates):
# The reference is a collage; the room photograph occupies x=.03-.94, y=.65-1.

#

#    increase the lens to fill the portrait image with the console and wall.

metal = (0.40, 0.39, 0.36)
yellow = (0.92, 0.67, 0.10)
red = (0.75, 0.025, 0.018)
amber = (0.96, 0.44, 0.025)

architecture = Asset("Architecture")
architecture.include("Floor", box((ROOM_W, ROOM_D, .12),
                                 (0, 0, -.06), floor_color))
architecture.include("Back_wall", box((ROOM_W, .12, ROOM_H),
                                     (0, 3.45, ROOM_H/2), wall))
architecture.include("Right_wall", box((.12, ROOM_D, ROOM_H),
                                      (4.95, 0, ROOM_H/2), wall))
architecture.include("Baseboard", box((ROOM_W, .05, .15),
                                      (0, 3.36, .075), base))

bank = Asset("Wall_instrument_bank")

                                 (-1.28, 3.30, 1.52), ivory))
for i in range(10):
    x = -4.55 + i * .70
    bank.include("Cabinet_joint_%02d" % i,
                 box((.014, .016, 2.45), (x, 3.205, 1.54), metal))
for col in list(range(5)) + list(range(8, 12)):
    x = -4.25 + col * .46
    for row in range(4):
        z = 1.05 + row * .42
        bank.include("Meter_frame_%02d_%02d" % (col, row),
                     box((.32, .035, .30), (x, 3.18, z), dark))
        bank.include("Meter_face_%02d_%02d" % (col, row),
                     box((.255, .014, .235), (x, 3.155, z), paper))
        bank.include("Meter_needle_%02d_%02d" % (col, row),
                     box((.012, .009, .085), (x+.025, 3.144, z), metal))
bank.include("Grille_mount", box((1.30, .04, .77),
                                 (-1.12, 3.16, 1.69), panel))
for i in range(8):
    bank.include("Vent_slot_%02d" % i,
                 box((1.16, .018, .036),
                     (-1.12, 3.13, 1.40+i*.075), dark))
scene.include("Wall_instrument_bank", bank)

# Main desk: dark supporting cabinet, horizontal writing surface, and sloped

desk.include("Dark_base", box((DESK_LENGTH, 1.55, .76),

desk.include("Writing_ledge", box((DESK_LENGTH, .43, .075),
                                 (DESK_CX, DESK_Y-.67, .85), paper))
desk.include("Ledge_front_trim", box((DESK_LENGTH, .035, .065),
                                    (DESK_CX, DESK_Y-.88, .84), dark))

face = box((DESK_LENGTH, 1.12, .085), (DESK_CX, face_y, face_z), panel)
face.turn(axis="x", degrees=slope)
desk.include("Inclined_control_surface", face)
a = math.radians(slope)
def surface(x, v, lift=.055):
    return (x, face_y + v*math.cos(a)-lift*math.sin(a),
            face_z + v*math.sin(a)+lift*math.cos(a))

for bay in range(8):

    seam = box((.018, 1.02, .01), surface(x-.35, 0), dark)
    seam.turn(axis="x", degrees=slope)
    desk.include("Panel_division_%02d" % bay, seam)
    # Three rows of knobs. Small dark control elements retain their spatial gaps.
    for row in range(3):
        for col in range(3):
            px = x-.21+col*.20
            v = -.34+row*.30
            p = surface(px, v, .065)
            desk.include("Knob_%02d_%02d_%02d" % (bay,row,col),
                         rod(.032, start=p,
                             end=(p[0],p[1]-.025,p[2]+.055), color=dark))
    # Wide pale meter at the back of alternate bays.
    if bay % 2 == 0:
        m = box((.35,.16,.018), surface(x,.42,.065), dark)
        m.turn(axis="x", degrees=slope)
        desk.include("Meter_rim_%02d" % bay, m)
        m = box((.28,.11,.02), surface(x,.42,.078), paper)
        m.turn(axis="x", degrees=slope)
        desk.include("Meter_face_%02d" % bay, m)

small.include("Inclined_face", sf)
for i in range(7):

        z = 1.00+(y-small_y)*math.tan(math.radians(22))+.07
        small.include("Control_%d_%d" % (i,j),

scene.include("Right_independent_console", small)

for i,z in enumerate((1.72,2.18,2.64)):

                 box((.64,.018,.035),(gx+.10,fy,z),dark))
    for side in (-1,1):
        x = gx+.10+side*.27
        grid.include("Branch_%d_%d" % (i,side),
                     box((.035,.018,.22),(x,fy,z+.09),dark))
        grid.include("Amber_lamp_%d_%d" % (i,side),
                     box((.095,.024,.095),(x,fy-.025,z+.09),amber))
for i in range(4):
    z = 1.68+i*.35
    grid.include("Red_lamp_%d" % i,
                 rod(.065,start=(gx-.40,fy-.02,z),
                     end=(gx-.40,fy-.07,z),color=red))
    grid.include("Selector_%d" % i,
                 rod(.040,start=(gx-.22,fy-.02,z),
                     end=(gx-.22,fy-.07,z),color=dark))
for i,z in enumerate((1.55,2.91)):
    grid.include("Label_plate_%d" % i,
```
